text:
alex: Heads up — customer jdoe reporting spikes of 502s + long tail latency on /v1/generate. They gave a request_id: req_0a1b2c and a minimal curl, but it's flaky.
customer-jdoe: repro: curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-1.0","input":"hello"}'
customer-jdoe: saw 502 once, then a 504, then 200. timestamps: ~2026-03-15T18:22:10Z
alex: Can you share full response headers + the raw request_id from the response? The header X-Req-Id or body request_id helps.
sara: Also ask them to run a short python/js/go minimal repro so we can narrow SDK vs network. Provide curl + SDK snippets we trust.
ryan: I'll grab logs if they give the request_id and approximate timestamp window. Also ask for a debug bundle: curl --header "X-Debug: true" to collect request dump.
support-bot: Reminder: for prod incidents include customer account id and whether they're on Dedicated/Hosted.
alex: Customer said hosted. ok. @customer-jdoe please run these and paste outputs: 1) curl -v with headers 2) python requests snippet 3) node fetch snippet 4) go net/http snippet
customer-jdoe: ok here's my curl verbose (trimmed):
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (3.12.45.67) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer ****
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< X-Req-Id: req_0a1b2c
< Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "bad gateway" }
alex: perfect — request id matches. @ryan can you pull gw logs around 18:22:00-18:24:00 UTC for req_0a1b2c? Also check any upstream timeouts.
ryan: grabbing logs now. quick tip for customer bundle: run curl with --trace-ascii dump.txt or set env REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 in SDKs to include debug headers.
sara: snippets to paste for customer (minimal):

Python:
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json={"model":"rwd-1.0","input":"hello"}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer TOKEN"}, timeout=30)
print(resp.status_code, resp.headers.get('X-Req-Id'), resp.text)
```

Node (fetch):
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',{ method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer TOKEN','Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-1.0', input:'hello'}) });
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('X-Req-Id'));
console.log(await res.text());
```

Go:
```go
client := &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
reqBody := bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"rwd-1.0","input":"hello"}`)
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", reqBody)
req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer TOKEN")
req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
res, _ := client.Do(req)
fmt.Println(res.StatusCode, res.Header.Get("X-Req-Id"))
```

sara: ask them to run each once and include both stdout and any trace file.
customer-jdoe: running now, will upload trace. also seeing this in browser devtools: timing blocked ~200ms, connect 30ms, waiting (TTFB) 2s then 502
alex: good details. once we have traces and req logs we'll correlate with gateway retries and backend qps. thanks all — @ryan ping when you have logs.
ryan: logs pulled: saw a 502 from gateway at 18:22:10 UTC, backend returned 502 because upstream returned 504 after 15s. attaching snippet: "upstream_status=504, upstream_time=15.02s". Looks like a backend model hotpath stall.
sara: recommend them to switch to smaller model variant while we root cause. also ask for any rate-limits on their side (concurrent clients).
customer-jdoe: uploaded trace.txt and python output. trace shows TCP resets right before 18:22:10.
alex: OK we'll open an internal ticket to dig into model queueing. for support record: issue_type: intermittent 502/504, affected_endpoint:/v1/generate, request_ids:["req_0a1b2c"], debug_bundle:uploaded, repro_snippets:provided.
support-bot: Case created: INC-2026-1123 assigned to eng-runtime.
alex: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with customer with ETA and temporary mitigation (smaller model / retry backoff).
